research.channel: Swiggy (food delivery, India) - data visible to a restaurant partner and to its POS/ERP (Petpooja / UrbanPiper-style integration)

Variants and add-ons chosen (options_to_add) with prices
Item-level taxes and item-level charges
data_points.notes: Swiggy quirk: taxes on item-level charges arrive in the order-level taxes array rather than on the item (seen in search snippet of UrbanPiper special-constraints page; page itself is paywalled to bots).

data_points.name: Swiggy service fee (commission) amount per order
data_points.via: Weekly payout annexure (order-level rows) only; NOT in the POS order relay
data_points.granularity: per order, but only after the payout cycle closes (weekly)
data_points.notes: The order relay schema has no commission/fee field. HelloBooks describes the annexure as carrying order-level gross value, commission, fees, adjustments, TDS. Petpooja's reconciliation shows per-order commission only after you upload the payout report (https://www.petpooja.com/poss/online-order-reconciliation). In the mock, live orders must show 'estimated commission' (contract % x gross) and only settled weeks should show 'actual'.

data_points.name: Collection (payment gateway) fee per order - 2%
data_points.notes: Deducted from payouts; not present in POS data. Exact annexure column name not verified from a public source.

data_points.granularity: per order in annexure / per invoice per cycle

data_points.name: Swiggy One per-order fee charged to restaurant (from 25 Nov 2025)

research.settlement_mechanics:
Cycle and lag: Swiggy settles restaurants weekly. Trade press (Verdict Foodservice, Nov 2025) states a weekly payout cadence, typically settling on Wednesdays or Thursdays, timing varying by city; orders of a Monday-Sunday week are therefore paid roughly 3-4 days after the week closes (so cash lag is about 3 to 10 days from order date). One third-party blog claims real-world lags of 10-14 days in 2026; treat that as anecdotal. An older source (2020) mentions weekly or bi-weekly depending on agreement. There is no evidence of a daily/T+1 restaurant payout option.

What is netted off before the bank credit (Swiggy collects 100% of customer money, including pay-on-delivery cash via its rider): (1) Service fee/commission as a contract % of GROSS order value - per Swiggy's own communication (Aug 2024) gross order value includes packaging charges and GST along with net order value, applied uniformly across metros and non-metros from 14 Aug 2024; commonly reported range 17-25%. (2) Collection fee of 2% of order value for online payment facilitation (standardised from 20 Dec 2023; a further rollout to additional restaurants from 16 Feb 2025). (3) GST at 18% on Swiggy's fees, covered by Swiggy's tax invoice. (4) Swiggy One per-order fee from 25 Nov 2025 (amount undisclosed; depends on the share of Swiggy One orders in the cycle). (5) Restaurant-funded share of discounts - shown in the annexure 'Discount Summary' with a 'Restaurant Share (%)' per campaign (100 = fully restaurant funded, 50 = co-funded); the Swiggy-funded share is not the restaurant's cost. (6) Ads and promotion charges - in the 'Other charges and deductions' sheet, which has one block for the current week and a second block for adjustments carried over from the previous week; real files contain rows such as 'Unable to fetch Campaign Details', and unauthorised ad deductions were widely reported in 2025-26. (7) Customer-complaint refunds and cancellation adjustments - Swiggy refunds the customer first and recovers from a later payout; dispute handling is via portal tickets. (8) TDS at 0.1% of the gross amount of sales facilitated (sec 194-O of the 1961 Act, reduced from 1% w.e.f. 1 Oct 2024; from 1 Apr 2026 the same rule sits in sec 393(1) Table Sl. 8(v) of the Income-tax Act 2025). It is a recoverable tax credit (Form 26AS), not an expense. (9) GST TCS under sec 52: not collected on restaurant services covered by sec 9(5) (CBIC Circular 167/23/2021); it applies only to non-9(5) supplies such as packaged MRP goods, at 0.5% since 10 Jul 2024.

Section 9(5) handling: since 1 Jan 2022 Swiggy is the deemed supplier for restaurant services sold through it. Swiggy charges the customer 5% GST, issues the invoice, and pays the tax to the government in cash; the restaurant does not charge, collect or receive this GST. In payout terms the customer-paid GST is included in the gross (and in the commission base) but is retained by Swiggy, so it appears as a deduction/pass-through and never reaches the bank. The restaurant still reports the taxable value in GSTR-3B Table 3.1.1(ii) and GSTR-1 Table 14 with no tax payable, and books its own sales net of that GST.

Visibility timing (the key modelling rule): per-order commission, collection fee, GST on fees, TDS and net payable exist only in the weekly annexure after the cycle closes; they are not in the live POS order payload and there is no settlement API (Petpooja's reconciliation relies on uploading the payout report). A truthful mock therefore shows 'estimated' fees for unsettled orders (contract rate x gross) and 'actual' figures only for settled weeks, with restaurant-level deductions (ads, carry-over adjustments) shown per week/outlet rather than per order.

caveats: Swiggy publishes almost no partner-facing documentation openly: partner.swiggy.com pages rendered empty to the fetcher, and merchant terms are behind login. Most findings rest on UrbanPiper's developer docs (strong for the POS payload), Swiggy's own blog (Market Intelligence Dashboard), Petpooja pages, trade press, and CA/reconciliation blogs.

Exact column headers of the Swiggy order-level annexure sheet could not be verified from any reachable public source (Scribd copies of real annexures refused connection). Only three sheet names are confirmed: Summary, Discount Summary (with 'Restaurant Share (%)'), Other charges and deductions. Use generic labels in the mock rather than pretending to replicate Swiggy's headers.

UrbanPiper helpjuice pages returned HTTP 402 to the fetcher; the statements 'Swiggy doesn't send its share of discount in the Order Relay payload' and 'every Swiggy order shows name Swiggy, email NA, phone 1234567890, address Bangalore' were taken from search-engine snippets of those pages, not a full page read.

Petpooja integrates with Swiggy directly rather than through UrbanPiper; I assumed Swiggy exposes the same data to all POS partners. Petpooja's own field-level documentation for Swiggy orders is not public, so customer-name masking inside Petpooja specifically is inferred, not confirmed.
Several restaurant blogs still quote TDS at 1%; that is outdated. The rate is 0.1% since 1 Oct 2024, and the section reference changed to 393(1) Sl. 8(v) from 1 Apr 2026. Use 0.1% in mock data.

Sources conflict on the commission base. Swiggy's Aug 2024 communication (Inc42, Business Standard) says service fee is on gross order value including GST and packaging; one blog says post-discount value. Whether 'gross' is before or after restaurant-funded discount is not settled by public sources - state the assumption in the mock.

Reports of a fixed per-order restaurant platform fee (Rs 5-15), standardised packaging deductions, rejection-rate threshold zones, and 10-14 day payout delays come from unsourced marketing blogs; treated as unclear.

Customer phone sharing with consent: as of Nov 2025 only Zomato had a consent prompt; Swiggy was in early talks with NRAI. I found no evidence of a Swiggy rollout by Sep 2026, but absence of evidence is not proof.

Funnel, ads, ratings, complaints and benchmark metrics are portal-only aggregates. An ERP can show them only if someone keys them in or uploads an export; the mock should label such tiles as 'source: Swiggy partner dashboard (manual/import)' and must not imply a live API feed.

Safe-to-show list for Swiggy in the mock: order and item sales, packaging, merchant-funded discounts, taxes (as pass-through), kitchen/rider timing derived from status timestamps, cancellations count, weekly settlement waterfall (gross -> commission -> collection fee -> GST on fees -> ads -> refunds/adjustments -> TDS -> net bank credit), estimated vs actual fees. Not safe: customer names/phones/addresses, repeat-customer cohorts, per-order new/repeat flags, delivery distance, customer delivery/platform fees, per-order ad attribution, payment-instrument split, live commission per order.

rate_corrections: Commission base is contract-specific, not 'uniform platform-wide': Inc42 says the Aug-2024 gross-value policy was extended to about 1,000 non-metro partners 'as of now'. Real annexures show a 'Service Fee Chargeable On' column equal to Net Bill Value (after merchant discount, incl. packaging) either without GST or plus GST on order. For mock maths use: base = item total + packaging - restaurant-funded discount + 5% GST; rate 17-25% stands (one real small-outlet file shows 24.0%); for a 5-outlet chain 20-22% is a defensible assumption (assumption, not sourced).

TDS: 0.1% (since 1 Oct 2024; sec 393(1) Table Sl. 8(v) from 1 Apr 2026) applied on Net Bill Value WITHOUT taxes, not on GST-inclusive gross - annexure glossary wording 'Charged at 1% on Net bill value (without taxes)' in a pre-Oct-2024 file.
Collection fee 2% stands (annexure line 'Payment Collection Charges'); the Feb-2025 Inc42 report says the email went only to select restaurants. One unsourced Scribd 'guide' claims 2.5% - ignore.
GST on Swiggy fees 18% stands (annexure formula text shows '*1.18').
TCS u/s 52: annexure shows 'TCS 0.0' for restaurant orders - keep nil.

Payout cadence: Sunday-Saturday period, 'Payout Settlement Date' = following Tuesday in real annexures (15-21 Sep 2024 -> 24 Sep; 8-14 Dec 2024 -> 17 Dec; 1-3 May 2025 -> 6 May); periods are cut at month-end. Verdict's 'Wednesdays or Thursdays' likely reflects bank-credit day. The researcher's Monday-Sunday assumption is not supported.

Swiggy Ads CPC: the cited agency page now states Rs 3-15 (not Rs 8-25); CPO Rs 35-55 for QSR/biryani and ROAS 4.5x-5.5x for QSR. All agency figures, low confidence; keep ad spend at roughly 3-6% of Swiggy GMV in the mock and label as illustrative.
Swiggy One restaurant fee: per-order from 25 Nov 2025, amount undisclosed, notified to 'select restaurant partners' - do not apply to every outlet by formula.
verify.notes:
Method and limits: the WebSearch budget for this session was already exhausted (200/200), so I searched through the Browser pane (Google/DuckDuckGo) and used WebFetch for page reads. Primary pages read directly: UrbanPiper order-relay and Swiggy feature-action docs, UrbanPiper help pages for the Swiggy channel, Swiggy's Market Intelligence blog, Swiggy Partner App Play Store and App Store listings, Petpooja reconciliation page and Petpooja 'Swiggy inside POS' blog (confirms embedded partner portal 'via a secure iframe', i.e. no API data), Inc42 (gross-value fee; 2% fee; MI dashboard), Verdict Foodservice (Swiggy One fee, 17-25%, weekly payout), Medianama (Nov 2025 data sharing: Swiggy only in talks; Apr 2026 unauthorised ad deductions incl. 'cost per sale' charges), TDSMAN, HelloBooks, dev.to annexure article and its companion guide (https://swiggy-consent-auditor.tool-template.workers.dev/guide). Scribd (real annexures) and UrbanPiper helpjuice were unreachable (connection refused / HTTP 402); all annexure column evidence therefore comes from search-engine snippets of those Scribd files, which is why I rate it medium, not high.
